stories.title: The pivot that never hit the inbox
stories.body: A client pivot is needed urgently. Instead of a chain of fragmented emails, the Creative Director and an analyst get together unprompted. They bring their specialisms to bear on the problem before it even reaches the client's inbox.

image.alt: Illustration of two colleagues working side by side at a desk with laptops

stories.title: We protect our own
stories.body: A team member is going through something difficult. Without being asked, teammates reorganise the day's heaviest work to give them space. Not because a manager told them to, but because we protect our own.

stories.title: Best results ever? Tell them today
stories.body: A new campaign we've launched has delivered the best results the client has ever seen. We don't quietly note it in the next report - we speak to them that afternoon, walk them through exactly what drove it, and use that insight to shape the future of the campaign.

stories.title: The full story of a new win
stories.body: We've just won a significant new client. Rather than a brief mention in the next company meeting, leadership shares the full story openly - who pitched, what won it, what it means commercially, and what it opens up for the team.

stories.title: Why the safe route is the risky one
stories.body: A client wants a safe campaign built on last year's benchmarks. Instead of taking the order, we show them why the safe route is actually the riskiest path to growth and push for a bolder approach. We lead the client; we don't just serve them.

image.alt: A team member working at a desk in front of a large monitor

stories.title: No more box-ticking
stories.body: A member of the team notices an internal process has become a box-ticking exercise with no real value. Rather than accepting it, they present a solution to the Senior Leadership Team. We don't wait for permission; we just make it better.

image.alt: A smiling team member in conversation with a colleague

stories.title: Three offices, one brief, one afternoon
stories.body: [Client name] needed a new approach by Friday. [Team member] in Leeds pulled in a strategist in Manchester and a designer in London, and they cracked it on one call. Nobody waited to be asked. The client saw a joined-up answer, not three separate ones.

stories.title: Cover without the ask
stories.body: [Team member] had a family emergency mid-sprint. By lunchtime, the team had split their workload and moved two deadlines with the client. Nobody made a fuss. They just made it work.

stories.title: The slide we moved to the front
stories.body: A key metric dipped for [Client name]. Instead of tucking it into the appendix, [Team member] led the monthly review with it, explained exactly why it happened and what we'd change. The client thanked us for the honesty and backed the new plan on the spot.

stories.title: "I don't know how to do this yet"
stories.body: [Team member] said it out loud in a team meeting. Within ten minutes, two people had offered to pair with them. That's what permission to fail looks like in real life.

stories.title: Changed my mind, gladly
stories.body: In a pitch rehearsal, [Team member] challenged the senior team's opening. Instead of defending it, they asked questions, listened, and rebuilt the first five minutes around the better idea.

stories.title: The test nobody asked for
stories.body: [Team member] spotted a gap in [Client name]'s search strategy and built a small test over a week, off their own back. It's now part of the client's plan for next quarter.

stories.title: We fixed onboarding. Again.
stories.body: New joiners kept asking the same questions in week one. [Team member] turned them into a simple guide, ran it past the People team and had it live within a fortnight.

stories.title: Shout-out to the night shift
stories.body: A launch for [Client name] slipped into the evening. [Team member] stayed on to check every link, then left a handover so clear the morning team could pick it up in five minutes.

stories.title: Bolder brief, better results
stories.body: [Client name] asked for a repeat of last year's campaign. The team came back with a braver idea and the evidence to support it. The client went for it.

stories.title: Feedback, the kind way
stories.body: [Team member] asked for honest feedback on their first client presentation. Their manager gave it straight, with three clear things to try next time, and sat in on the next one to help.

incoming.title: Hackathon to handover in a day
incoming.body: [Team member] ran a lunchtime AI hack with four people from three teams. By the end of the day they had a working prototype to speed up client reporting, and a plan to test it properly.

incoming.title: Quiet voice, big idea
incoming.body: [Team member] doesn't often speak up in big meetings, so their manager asked for their view first. It reshaped the whole plan for [Client name].
